title: Temporal Gradient Inversion for Private Trajectory Reconstruction in Embodied Reinforcement Learning
why_read: A privacy-attack paper demonstrating that even gradient-only distributed learning in robots leaks private sensor trajectories, relevant to anyone building federated or distributed RL systems.
analysis: The paper shows that in distributed reinforcement learning setups where only gradients (not raw data) are sent to a server, an attacker can still reconstruct sequences of private observations and actions by exploiting correlations across time steps. Their attack, called TRACE, works fast, at a few milliseconds per frame, and gets much better reconstruction quality than previous single-frame gradient inversion attacks. This has real implications for embodied AI and robotics systems that assume gradient sharing alone is privacy-preserving. The defense implication, that privacy protections need to consider sequences rather than isolated updates, is a useful practical takeaway.
